title: By a Single Point: Sonny Survives Kai's Comeback Bid as Three Unbeatens Become a Real Race
dek: The Horse is Hea stayed perfect by one point over the Dawgs, HULK kept bulldozing, and Randy did something nobody thought he would: he made a trade.
body: One point. That was the whole difference between Sonny staying perfect and Sonny joining the pile of 1-loss teams wondering what went wrong. The Horse is Hea edged Mekhi's Dawgs 122.7 to 121.7 in the closest game of the season, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the reason again, turning a 17.19 projection into 30.36 points one week after his 38-point explosion. The computer, which spent two weeks shrugging at the commissioner, finally bought in: Sonny's title odds more than doubled from 10% to 21%, good for second in the league. It wasn't pretty, but a 3-0 record doesn't come with style points.

The loss belongs in the Kai hall of near-misses, and it hurts more because he did so much right. The waiver-wire king grabbed Tyler Shough this week, cutting Jameson Williams to make room, and Shough repaid him immediately with 23.8 points. Then the rest of the lineup page happened: Brock Bowers scored 22.6 from the Dawgs' bench, and Justin Jefferson managed just 4.2 against a 14.79 projection. When you lose by a single point with a 22-point tight end watching from the sideline, that's a week that lingers. Mekhi is 0-3, but his 320.8 points are more than Kaushal's, and his playoff odds sit at 13%.

No Banner only HULK, meanwhile, did what it does. Ramon put 134.46 on Kaushal's Habibsters, winning by 33.72 as a 77% favorite, and he once again had a starting-caliber quarterback in reserve, with Matthew Stafford scoring 20.9 on the bench. HULK now has 444.2 points, 72.6 more than anyone else in the league. Strangely, the title odds slipped from 54% to 52%, which is the algorithm's way of saying it's nitpicking because it can't find anything else to criticize. Brucie remains the best team in the league and the most annoying fact in everyone else's week.

Habibi got a big game from Drake London, 23.9 points on a 12.52 projection, and it barely mattered. The two-time champ is 0-3 with 12% playoff odds and spent the week remodeling again: the 49ers D/ST in for the Buccaneers, Deebo Samuel Sr. in for kicker Jake Bates, and Wan'Dale Robinson out for Sam LaPorta, the same tight end Alan cut a week ago. Picking up the villain's leftovers is a bold strategy. Kaushal has won this league twice by moving fast, and right now he's flooring it just to get out of the basement.

Speaking of the villain, Alan is officially rolling. Team Pillbert beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 117.88 to 100.98 behind a monster backfield-and-quarterback combo: Jahmyr Gibbs posted the week's best line at 37.9 and Brock Purdy added 31.28, a combined 69.18 points from two guys. It could have been even uglier, since De'Von Achane flopped with 1.7 points while Harold Fannin Jr. scored 20.6 on the bench. Despite the win, Philliberto's title odds slid from 13% to 9%, and you can bet he'll treat that as a personal insult. He also churned the roster, adding Bryce Young and Denzel Boston while cutting Jaxson Dart and the Lions D/ST.

JMoney's side of that game is a small step forward that still lands as a loss. His 100.98 was Counting or not Counting GV's first triple-digit score of the season, a clear improvement on the 75.96 and 82.08 that came before it, but it runs his record to 0-3 with 1% playoff odds. He went shopping too, picking up Tank Bigsby and swapping the Eagles D/ST for the Patriots D/ST. In a twist, the commissioner promptly scooped up those Eagles, which means Jordan's castoffs are now playing for an undefeated team.

Randy's The fumblers got past Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 91.64 to 86.64 in the week's lowest-scoring game, taking round one of the league's Bears-versus-Packers border war. Zilgit nearly stole it as a 32% underdog thanks to Bijan Robinson's 34.3 points, nearly double his projection, while Jonathan Taylor gave Randy just 8.2 on a 19.1 projection. Zoe is 1-2 and still learning fast, reshaping her roster with Josh Downs for Brian Thomas Jr., Blake Corum for Jonathon Brooks, and Trey Smack for Cairo Santos at kicker. Randy is 3-0, but like Alan, his win came with a projection haircut: title odds fell from 21% to 16%.

Then came the news that stopped the group chat: Randy made a trade. The league's tightest grip sent Javonte Williams to Alan for Stefon Diggs, proof that it can be done. The other deal is just as juicy, as Sonny sent Chuba Hubbard's counterpart Rashee Rice... correction from the trade log: Sonny received Chuba Hubbard and sent Rashee Rice to Ramon, the commissioner doing business with the league's runaway favorite. Week 4 brings the villain summit, Alan's Team Pillbert against Ramon's HULK, plus Zoe getting her shot at the commissioner's perfect record, Randy against a desperate Kaushal, and a Dawgs-versus-Counting or not Counting GV game where one 0-3 team finally gets off the mat.

social.text: Lost by ONE point. Brock Bowers scored 22.6 on our bench. We are not okay. We will be watching the waiver wire with Kai at dawn.

social.author: Numbers Don't Lie Guy
social.text: HULK: 444.2 points through 3 weeks. Next closest: 371.6. That gap is bigger than some teams' weekly scores.

social.author: Gibbs Gang
social.text: Gibbs 37.9. Purdy 31.28. Team Pillbert wins and the computer drops his title odds anyway. The machine fears the bad guy too.

bios.1: The defending champ is 3-0 after surviving Mekhi by a single point, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba carrying the offense for a second straight week. Sonny's title odds jumped from 10% to 21%, and he reshaped the roster with Chuba Hubbard via trade and Jordan's old Eagles D/ST off waivers. Zoe gets the next crack at his perfect record.
bios.2: Randy is 3-0 after grinding out a 91.64 win over Zoe, though Jonathan Taylor's 8.2 points made it closer than it needed to be. The bigger news: he actually traded, sending Javonte Williams to Alan for Stefon Diggs. Title odds dipped to 16%, but playoff odds sit at a sturdy 92%.
bios.3: Jordan is 0-3 but posted his first 100-point week, a 100.98 that showed real progress even in a loss to Alan. He added Tank Bigsby and the Patriots D/ST as he tries to build a roster that can keep that pace. Playoff odds are at 1%, and a home date with the 0-3 Dawgs is his best shot at a first win.
bios.4: Alan is 2-1 and riding a two-game win streak after Jahmyr Gibbs and Brock Purdy combined for 69.18 points against Jordan. He's been working every angle, adding Bryce Young, Denzel Boston, and Javonte Williams this week. His title odds slipped to 9%, and next week he takes on the unbeaten HULK.
bios.5: Mekhi is 0-3 after the cruelest loss of the season, a one-point defeat with Brock Bowers scoring 22.6 on the bench. His Tyler Shough pickup hit right away, and his 320.8 points suggest the record is worse than the roster. A matchup with fellow 0-3 Jordan is the best chance yet to get on the board.
bios.6: The two-time champ is 0-3 after running into HULK, despite 23.9 points from Drake London. Kaushal remade the roster again, adding Sam LaPorta, Deebo Samuel Sr., and the 49ers D/ST. Playoff odds sit at 12%, and Randy's unbeaten squad is next.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 3-0 with 444.2 points, more than 70 clear of the field, and has 100% playoff odds and 52% title odds. Brucie keeps winning with real points stuck on his bench, and he just added Rashee Rice in a deal with the commissioner. Next up is a villain-on-villain showdown with Alan.
bios.8: Zoe is 1-2 after a five-point loss to Randy in which Bijan Robinson nearly carried her on his own with 34.3. The rookie is churning the roster with confidence, bringing in Josh Downs, Blake Corum, and Trey Smack. She sits fifth with 10% playoff odds and draws the 3-0 commissioner next.
